title: Team Members Who Hide the Ball
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece describes ambitious team members who withhold negative information to protect their image and preserve their autonomy, a behavior the author says leaders often unintentionally reward by celebrating only good news. Once a leader gets involved after negative information surfaces, ambitious team members lose latitude they'd rather keep, so they bury problems instead. The recommended fix is building shared visibility -- dashboards, team check-ins, open debate -- rather than relying on one-on-one updates, and explicitly praising people for surfacing problems early rather than only for good news.
points: Ambitious team members often hide negative information specifically to preserve their autonomy, since surfacing problems invites leader involvement.
Leaders who celebrate only good news unintentionally teach team members that bad news is unwelcome.
Relying on one-on-one updates makes leaders more susceptible to being managed by selectively-sharing team members.
Shared visibility -- dashboards, team check-ins, open debate -- makes it much harder for any individual to filter information.
quotes: They hide the ball to project the positive image they want to burnish in their leader’s mind.
This behavior is often unintentionally rewarded, as leaders who prefer good news make a fuss over the good news they hear.
Ambitious team members loathe the idea of losing that latitude, so they keep problems to themselves and hope no one notices.
The better practice is to create shared visibility through dashboards, team check-ins, and open debate. This makes it much harder for any single individual to filter or control information.
Good leaders know trust and performance die in the dark. They demand visibility and shared truth.
